standard_prerequisites.name: Pro-objects of modules and morphisms between them
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the final conclusion at statement lines 29455-29456
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the sense in which (H_n) and (I^nH) are isomorphic.

core_obligations: Rewrite H_n as (Ker(beta) cap I^nL)/alpha(I^nK) and obtain the maps H_n -> H_{n-1} and H_1 -> H from the inclusions Ker(beta) cap I^nL in Ker(beta) cap I^{n-1}L and alpha(I^nK) in alpha(I^{n-1}K) (proof lines 29460-29463).

Apply Artin-Rees twice to choose c_1 and c_2 with Im(alpha) cap I^nL contained in alpha(I^{n-c_1}K) for n >= c_1 and Ker(beta) cap I^nL contained in I^{n-c_2}Ker(beta) for n >= c_2, and set c = c_1 + c_2 (proof lines 29466-29470).
Deduce from c >= c_2 that for n >= c the image of H_n -> H is contained in I^{n-c}H (proof lines 29473-29474).
For n >= c define psi_n : I^nH -> H_{n-c} by choosing y in I^n Ker(beta) representing x and taking its class in H_{n-c} (proof lines 29477-29479).

Prove well-definedness: a second representative y' differs from y by an element of Im(alpha), which by c >= c_1 lies in alpha(I^{n-c}K), so y and y' have the same class in H_{n-c} (proof lines 29480-29482 and following).
Conclude that the two displayed compositions are the canonical maps and hence that (H_n) and (I^nH) are isomorphic as pro-objects of the category of modules (statement conclusion).
difficulty_reason: This is the companion of the Artin-Rees consequence for a complex of finite modules over a Noetherian ring, with the I-adic filtration applied to the terms rather than the quotients: for the induced complex I^nK -> I^nL -> I^nM with homology H_n the lemma produces canonical maps and a constant c such that the image of H_n -> H lies in I^{n-c}H, together with a canonical map I^nH -> H_{n-c} making the two displayed compositions canonical, so that the inverse systems (H_n) and (I^nH) are isomorphic as pro-objects (source lines 29431-29457). The proof rewrites H_n as (Ker(beta) cap I^nL)/alpha(I^nK), gets the comparison maps from the two inclusions, and again applies Artin-Rees twice to choose c_1 and c_2 so that Im(alpha) cap I^nL lies in alpha(I^{n-c_1}K) and Ker(beta) cap I^nL lies in I^{n-c_2}Ker(beta), setting c = c_1 + c_2 (proof lines 29460-29470). It then defines psi_n : I^nH -> H_{n-c} by choosing a representative y in I^n Ker(beta) and proves well-definedness using that a second representative differs by an element of Im(alpha), which by the choice of c_1 lies in alpha(I^{n-c}K) (proof lines 29477-29482 and following). The non-routine content is again the pair of Artin-Rees constants and the well-definedness check.
